briefs.problem: At a fixed-date, in-person event, there is no reliable way to identify arriving attendees, record their entry, and produce accurate post-event attendance data — leaving door queues and data gaps as the likely failure mode.
briefs.solution: A staff-operated check-in app that identifies attendees at the entrance, records arrivals (and possibly zone/session access), and produces an attendance record for after the event.

challenges.headline: Single-event assumption unexamined
challenges.premise: The request reads as a one-off build for this event, with no mention of reuse.
challenges.alternative: Deciding now whether this is the first instance of a reusable event kit — even a lightweight config layer for categories, zones, and branding — costs little at this stage but is expensive to retrofit once the data model is fixed.
challenges.consequence: Building as pure one-off and discovering later that more events are planned means redoing the attendee/category/zone model from scratch under a new fixed date.
challenges.recommendation: Ask the client directly whether more events are planned before committing to the data model.

challenges.headline: Connectivity assumed reliable
challenges.premise: The request implies staff simply scan a badge, with no mention of venue network conditions.
challenges.alternative: Treating the app as offline-first by default — local snapshot of the attendee list, check-ins synced later with conflict rules — removes the single biggest failure risk at the door.
challenges.consequence: An online-only build that meets a saturated-wifi venue on the day fails visibly, in front of the client, with no way to recover before the event ends.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm venue connectivity (ideally via a site visit) before locking the architecture, and default to offline-capable unless proven unnecessary.

challenges.headline: Check-in treated as boolean
challenges.premise: The request describes 'check-in' as a single action per attendee, with no distinction of duplicate, re-entry, or zone access.
challenges.alternative: Modeling check-in as an event log per attendee per zone/session — rather than a single flag — handles re-entry and multi-zone access without a data-model rewrite.
challenges.consequence: A naive single-flag model breaks the first time two devices scan the same attendee within seconds, or a VIP needs access to more than one zone.
challenges.recommendation: Pin down the intended semantics (duplicate vs. re-entry vs. zone access) before building the data model, not after concurrency testing surfaces the gap.

challenges.headline: Assuming reliable venue connectivity
challenges.premise: The request implies staff will simply scan attendees at the entrance, with no mention of what happens if the network drops.
challenges.alternative: Design for offline-first: a local snapshot of the attendee list on each device, check-ins queued and synced when connectivity returns, with a defined conflict-resolution rule.
challenges.consequence: If built online-only, a wifi dead zone or saturated network on the day stops check-in entirely, in front of the client, with no way to fix it before the event ends.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm connectivity expectations and test the actual venue network before committing to an architecture.

challenges.headline: Treating the attendee list as frozen
challenges.premise: The request describes checking attendees in against a list, without addressing how that list is built or kept current.
challenges.alternative: Support on-site additions and corrections (walk-ins, name changes, substitutions) as a first-class path, not an import exception.
challenges.consequence: If the app assumes a frozen import, staff will be stuck at the door every time a name doesn't match exactly what was registered.
challenges.recommendation: Clarify the registration source and require an on-site edit/add capability before build.

challenges.headline: Undefined duplicate-scan behavior
challenges.premise: Checking someone in is treated as a single, unambiguous action.
challenges.alternative: Explicitly model duplicate (block), re-entry (allow), and different-zone (record separately) as three distinct outcomes, decided per client rule, not assumed.
challenges.consequence: Without this, the first double-scan across two doors within seconds will either wrongly block a legitimate attendee or silently double-count arrivals.
challenges.recommendation: Settle this rule with the client before touching the data model — it changes what a 'check-in' record actually is.

challenges.headline: One-off build vs. reusable kit
challenges.premise: The request is scoped as a single app for this event, with no mention of future events.
challenges.alternative: Parameterizing the event/attendee/zone model now, even minimally, costs little extra and avoids a rebuild if this client runs events again.

challenges.headline: Connectivity assumed reliable
challenges.premise: The request describes a clean scan action with no mention of what happens if the connection drops.
challenges.alternative: A local snapshot of the attendee list with queued, eventually-synced check-ins keeps the door moving regardless of venue wifi quality.
challenges.consequence: If the app is built online-only and the venue has the dead zones typical of conference spaces, check-in fails visibly in front of the client during the busiest twenty minutes of the day.
challenges.recommendation: Settle offline vs. online-only as an architecture decision before writing the check-in flow, not as a later setting.

challenges.headline: Repeat scan meaning undefined

challenges.consequence: Left undefined, a naive 'block on second scan' will wrongly refuse legitimate re-entries or multi-zone attendees the first time two staff scan the same person from different doors.
challenges.recommendation: Get the client to define the three cases explicitly and confirm which zones/sessions require separate check-ins.

decisions.decision: Check-in records reference an Attendee (with a Category) as the core business object

exclusions.option: Fully generalizing into a multi-event reusable kit in this phase
exclusions.reason: The event date is fixed and non-negotiable, and reuse hasn't been confirmed yet — investing in full generalization now risks the one deadline that matters before knowing it will pay off.

exclusions.option: Integrating directly with a registration/ticketing system as part of this build
exclusions.reason: The current process feeding the attendee list isn't established, and adding a live integration under a fixed date is scope the timeline likely can't absorb.

thresholds.condition: The client confirms this is the first of several events, not a one-off
thresholds.measure: answer to the single-event vs. reusable-kit question
thresholds.action: invest in generalizing the offline-sync engine and attendee/zone model into a shared event kit

thresholds.condition: On-site network testing at the actual venue shows reliable coverage throughout
thresholds.measure: connectivity test results at the venue
thresholds.action: simplify to an online-only architecture and drop the offline sync layer

open_decisions: Exact rule for duplicate vs. re-entry vs. zone-specific check-in
Source of the attendee list and the on-site editing workflow for walk-ins/corrections
Target throughput per attendee and acceptable failure rate at peak arrival
Rehearsal and rollout plan for event day
